--- title: "Are we sure the model is correctly using the NACA 0006 airfoil?" --- The section is checked three ways — that the geometry is what it claims, that every surface carries it, and that NeuralFoil returns a symmetric polar from it — and then the choice itself is tested by giving each surface the section its own chords imply. ::: {.callout-note} ## Assumed Matching a surface to its own t/c means picking a NACA section of that thickness. That is the nearest available stand-in, not the same thing as a square-cut plate — which is the point the answer turns on. ::: ::: {#84ff4f6c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} af = asb.Airfoil("naca0006") print(f"max thickness {af.max_thickness():.4f}, max camber {af.max_camber():.6f}") for w in mceagle.wings: print(f"{w.name:11s} sections carry {set(x.airfoil.name for x in w.xsecs)}") a2 = np.linspace(-4, 4, 9) for Re in [1.6e3, 3.6e4]: # the fin tip, and the mean chord r = af.get_aero_from_neuralfoil(alpha=a2, Re=Re) print(f"Re {Re:7.0f}: CL(0) {np.array(r['CL'])[4]:+.2e}, " f"dCL/dalpha {np.polyfit(a2, np.array(r['CL']), 1)[0]:.4f} /deg " f"(thin-airfoil 0.1097), confidence " f"{float(np.array(r['analysis_confidence'])[0]):.2f}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` max thickness 0.0600, max camber 0.000000 Wing sections carry {'naca0006'} Stabilizer sections carry {'naca0006'} Fin sections carry {'naca0006'} Re 1600: CL(0) +1.11e-16, dCL/dalpha 0.0780 /deg (thin-airfoil 0.1097), confidence 0.94 Re 36000: CL(0) +1.38e-16, dCL/dalpha 0.0981 /deg (thin-airfoil 0.1097), confidence 0.98 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#6941e0c5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} tc = {} for nm, etas, chords in [("wing", wing_eta, wing_c), ("stab", stab_eta, stab_c), ("fin", fin_eta, fin_c)]: t = t_foam / chords * 100 tc[nm] = np.trapezoid(t * chords, etas) / np.trapezoid(chords, etas) # Lift-curve slope against thickness, at the fin's own Reynolds number. slope = {} for nm in ["naca0006", "naca0008", "naca0010", "naca0013"]: r = asb.Airfoil(nm).get_aero_from_neuralfoil(alpha=a2, Re=1.56e4) slope[nm] = np.polyfit(a2, np.array(r["CL"]), 1)[0] ``` ::: ::: {#67727a4b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} def swap(af_w, af_h, af_v): """The airframe rebuilt with a chosen section on each surface.""" xs = lambda le, eta, c, af, **kw: asb.WingXSec(xyz_le=le, chord=c, airfoil=af, **kw) return asb.Airplane( name="v", fuselages=mceagle.fuselages, s_ref=S_w, c_ref=c_w, b_ref=b_w, xyz_ref=[x_qc_w, 0, 0], wings=[ asb.Wing(name="Wing", symmetric=True, xsecs=[ xs([x_le_w, e*b_w/2, e*z_tip], e, c, af_w) for e, c in zip(wing_eta, wing_c)]), asb.Wing(name="Stabilizer", symmetric=True, xsecs=[ xs([x_le_h, e*b_h/2, z_h], e, c, af_h, twist=i_h) for e, c in zip(stab_eta, stab_c)]), asb.Wing(name="Fin", xsecs=[ xs([x_te_v - c, 0, e*b_v], e, c, af_v) for e, c in zip(fin_eta, fin_c)]), ]) mp0 = mass_properties() def Cn_beta(ap, alpha=4.0, V=6.0): """Directional stability, about the airplane's own moment reference.""" d = asb.AeroBuildup( airplane=ap, op_point=asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=V, alpha=alpha) ).run_with_stability_derivatives(alpha=False, p=False, q=False, r=False) return float(np.array(d["Cnb"]).ravel()[0]) matched = swap(*map(asb.Airfoil, ["naca0006", "naca0008", "naca0013"])) arms = {} for label, ap in [("all 0006, as modelled", mceagle), ("stab 0008, fin 0013", matched)]: x_np = neutral_point(ap) arms[label] = (x_np, ballast_for(x_np - 0.10 * c_w, 0.0, mp0), Cn_beta(ap)) # Cn_beta above is about the model's moment reference at the wing quarter-chord. # The aircraft does not pivot there -- it pivots about its CG, which ballasting # puts further aft, shortening the fin's arm. Same airframe, moved reference. x_cg_10 = arms["all 0006, as modelled"][0] - 0.10 * c_w about_cg = asb.Airplane( name="v", wings=mceagle.wings, fuselages=mceagle.fuselages, s_ref=S_w, c_ref=c_w, b_ref=b_w, xyz_ref=[x_cg_10, 0, 0], ) Cnb_about_cg = Cn_beta(about_cg) ``` ::: **Answer.** Yes, mechanically. The geometry is a true NACA 0006 — 6\.00% thick, zero camber — every section of all three surfaces carries it, and NeuralFoil returns CL(0) = 0 to machine precision with a slope near thin-airfoil theory, still at high confidence down at the fin tip's Re of 1,600. What is not right is the reason recorded for choosing it. Six percent matches the wing's mean chord and nothing else: the same 5 mm foam is 7\.9% of the stabilizer's chord and 12\.8% of the fin's (@tbl-tc). Matching those makes the model worse. NeuralFoil's smooth sections shed lift-curve slope quickly at this scale (@tbl-thickness) — so a 13% fin flips Cn_beta from \+0\.0975 to \-0\.0103 and the aircraft loses directional stability. A square-cut plate does not behave that way, because its sharp edge fixes separation and reattachment. One thin section on every surface is therefore the right model of a flat plate, and being thinner than the tail's true t/c is the point rather than an error. One consequence for later work: the Cn_beta above is taken about the model's moment reference at the wing quarter-chord, 118\.1 mm. About the ballasted CG at 149\.0 mm it is \+0\.0498 /rad — 51% of the figure quoted above, because the fin's arm is shorter from there. ::: {#tbl-tc .cell tbl-cap='What 5 mm of foam is worth as a thickness ratio on each surface, against the 6% every surface is modelled at.' execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd pd.DataFrame({ "surface": list(tc), "area-weighted t/c [%]": [f"{v:.1f}" for v in tc.values()], "modelled as [%]": ["6.0"] * len(tc), }).style.hide(axis="index") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The method, as called ```python def neutral_point(airplane=None, band=(0.0, 8.0), V=6.0): """ Neutral point [m aft of the nose], from a straight-line fit of Cm vs CL. The moment reference is read off the airplane rather than passed in. AeroBuildup reports Cm about `xyz_ref`, and the answer is only meaningful measured from that same station; sourcing the two separately silently biases the result by the offset between them, which is exactly the error that inflated the wing-station sensitivity in the assumptions entry. This is one of the few places worth NOT using the library's own function. `run_with_stability_derivatives()` returns x_np from the identical formula, but by finite-differencing at a point; at this Reynolds number Cm against CL is genuinely curved, so that answer moves with the angle you take it at -- 147 to 197 mm across the same band. This returns the average slope over a stated range instead. Neither removes the choice, so `band` is an explicit argument every entry declares. See the entry on using AeroSandbox's x_np. """ ap = mceagle if airplane is None else airplane p = polars(ALPHA_SWEEP, V=V, airplane=ap) CL, Cm = np.array(p["CL"]), np.array(p["Cm"]) k = (ALPHA_SWEEP >= band[0]) & (ALPHA_SWEEP <= band[1]) return ap.xyz_ref[0] - np.polyfit(CL[k], Cm[k], 1)[0] * c_w def ballast_for(x_cg_target, x_ballast=0.0, mp=None): """ Point mass [kg] at `x_ballast` that moves the CG to `x_cg_target`. The CG of structure plus ballast is a mass-weighted mean, so the mass needed follows from the lever ratio. Defaults to the unballasted airframe. """ m = mass_properties() if mp is None else mp return m.mass * (m.x_cg - x_cg_target) / (x_cg_target - x_ballast) ``` :::
